open_obligations: Check the EAS-ASD trend for the Debate configurations and whether it is statistically significant for the authors' sample of questions and agents
Check that EAS is a reasonable analogue of Khan et al.'s debater aggregate rating and ASD of their judge accuracy
out.other_title: Self-play debate: judge accuracy rises with debater aggregate rating
out.rationale: Khan et al. report a strong correlation between judge accuracy and debater aggregate rating in self-play debates judged by GPT-4-Turbo: as debaters are optimised against win rate, judge accuracy improves. The authors report that in Debate higher EAS is associated with higher ASD. They call it a reproduction of Khan et al.'s finding, but with new, more general metrics (EAS and ASD rather than aggregate rating and judge accuracy), so it is recorded as SUPPORTS rather than REPLICATES.
out.scope: proposed SUPPORTS: Whether more capable or persuasive debaters make debate favour the true answer more; holds for Debate in the authors' setup.

text: The authors say they reproduce the finding of Khan et al. (2024) with their new, more general metrics: in Debate, higher EAS is associated with higher ASD. They suggest Debate will continue to incentivize alignment as capabilities scale, though this is not a formal guarantee for the superhuman regime.
